name: JS Clock Sky
description: JavaScript node demo: the real time of day drives the sky. The JS reads Date(), computes sun and moon directions, the moon phase and the turn of the stars, and draws a clock into a canvas; a GLSL node paints the sky looking south over hills (golden hour, phased moon, stars, clouds, town lights). Time speed fast-forwards. Tweak it in the Parameters panel (P): Time and Sky.

data.text:
# JS Clock Sky
The sky outside your window, right now: a JavaScript node reads the clock with Date() and turns the local time into sun and moon directions, the moon phase and the turn of the stars; a GLSL node paints the sky looking south over hills.
Fast-forward with Time speed (1 = real time, 3600 = an hour per second) to watch sunsets, starry nights and the moon rise.
## What the JS does
- Every frame: hour = now + Hour offset + fast-forwarded hours (state.ff += dt × (speed − 1) / 3600, so speeding up never jumps).
- Sun: declination from the day of the year, hour angle from the hour, latitude from the param → sunDir (x = east, y = up, z = north).
- Moon: phase from a known new moon and the 29.53-day synodic month; it trails the sun by phase × 24 h → moonDir, moonPhase.
- Clock: a 512×160 canvas with HH:MM and the moon phase name, redrawn once a minute (a canvas texture output).
- Outputs: sunDir, moonDir, moonPhase, pole, starTurn, clock, hour.
## Make it yours
Double-click the JS node (Clock group): add a sunrise alarm, use your exact longitude for true solar time, or fetch the weather in setup (await fetch(...)) and drive the Clouds from it. Clock Sky (Sky group) is plain GLSL.
## Tweak it in the Parameters panel
Press P: Time and Sky settings; hover a name for what it does, double-click a slider to reset it.
Double-click a group box to open it, Esc to come back.

## Clock (JS)
Reads params['Time speed'], ['Hour offset'], ['Latitude'] by label, Date() and dt.
All directions are in a local frame: x = east, y = up, z = north. The camera looks south.

## Sky
Clock Sky: day/night gradient, golden and blue hour toward the sun, sun disc and halo, phased moon with craters, stars turning around the pole, drifting clouds lit by sun / dusk / moon, hills with town lights at night, and the clock canvas in the corner. Then ACES, vignette and grain.
